facebook.long_form:
🚨 THE WAIT IS OVER — KAWHI IS GOING BACK TO TORONTO 🚨

The NBA has officially cleared the LA Clippers of cap circumvention in the Aspiration investigation, and that clears the path for one of the most emotionally charged trades of the 2026 offseason to be finalized.

Kawhi Leonard — the man who hit the iconic corner four in Game 7 against Philadelphia, the man who carried Toronto to its first and only NBA championship in 2019, winning Finals MVP — is headed back to the Raptors.

In exchange, the Clippers receive Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, and draft compensation.

The investigation had centered on whether the Clippers had used sponsorship arrangements through Aspiration (now bankrupt) to pay Leonard in a way that circumvented the salary cap. The NBA looked into it, and the Clippers have been cleared.

What does this mean for the Raptors? Kawhi is 35, and this isn't a rebuild situation — this is an experienced winner who knows what a championship feels like in Toronto. Training camp opens September 28. The Raptors and their fans have been waiting all summer. That wait is now officially over.

Drop a 🦖 if you're hyped for Kawhi's Toronto homecoming!

facebook.long_form:
⏰ THE STEPHEN CURRY EXTENSION DEADLINE IS TOMORROW ⏰

August 29, 2026. That's the day Stephen Curry becomes eligible to sign a contract extension with the Golden State Warriors — and the entire basketball world will be watching.

Here's where things stand:

✅ WARRIORS GM MIKE DUNLEAVY JR. is "pretty confident" Curry will finish his career in Golden State. The organization is ready to offer the two-year, $136.7 million maximum extension.

⚠️ ESPN'S BRIAN WINDHORST says Curry should pump the brakes. The logic: if Curry takes a shorter-term deal (reportedly a 1-year, $62.6M structure has been discussed), the Warriors could have up to $100 million in cap flexibility — enough to land another star alongside Steph and potentially end the franchise's championship drought.

The Warriors went 37-45 last season. Steph is 38 years old and still one of the greatest players on the planet. Does he bet on himself with a shorter deal to bring in more help — or does he accept the max and trust the organization to build around him?

Tomorrow we find out.

What do YOU think Steph should do? 👇

facebook.long_form:
🇫🇷 WEMBY WENT OFF — AND FRANCE IS ROLLING 🇫🇷

Victor Wembanyama, the reigning NBA Defensive Player of the Year and San Antonio Spurs star, posted 22 points and 9 rebounds Thursday night as France defeated Slovenia in FIBA World Cup qualifying play.

France is now 6-1 in Group L. Next up: Sweden on August 30.

Wembanyama, who was named France's captain for this qualifying window, made headlines earlier with a quote that stuck: "I do not miss the NBA right now. I miss FIBA basketball." And he's backing it up on the court.

This is a guy who averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, and 3.1 blocks per game for San Antonio last season while winning DPOY — and he's using his offseason to represent his country with the same level of intensity.

With France looking like a serious contender in European qualifying, the 2027 FIBA World Cup picture is starting to come into focus. And Wemby is making sure France is in the conversation.

facebook.long_form:
💔 TOUGH NEWS FOR THE PORTLAND TRAIL BLAZERS — SHAEDON SHARPE IS OUT.

Portland Trail Blazers guard Shaedon Sharpe has suffered a torn right meniscus and is expected to miss approximately six months, putting his expected return around late February 2027.

Last season, Sharpe was having the best year of his professional career — averaging a career-high 20.8 points per game and cementing himself as one of the most exciting young players in the league. This injury couldn't have come at a worse time.

The Blazers this offseason acquired Ja Morant from Memphis — an All-Star guard who was supposed to be paired with Sharpe as Portland's dynamic backcourt duo of the future. Now, Morant will carry the scoring load alone as the Blazers begin a new chapter in their rebuild.

Wishing Shaedon a full and fast recovery. 🙏

facebook.long_form:
🏀 NBA OPENING NIGHT IS GOING TO BE ABSOLUTELY ELECTRIC 🏀

Mark your calendars: October 20, 2026. The NBA returns with a three-game showcase that might be the most anticipated Opening Night in a generation.

Here's what's on tap:

🎯 GAME 1 — Boston Celtics at Detroit Pistons, 3 PM ET (NBC)
🏆 GAME 2 — Philadelphia 76ers at New York Knicks, 7 PM ET (NBC)
🌩️ GAME 3 — Oklahoma City Thunder at San Antonio Spurs, 9:30 PM ET (NBC)

The centerpiece? The Knicks — NBA Champions — will hang their first banner at Madison Square Garden since 1973 before hosting a 76ers team loaded to the gills with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, alongside Joel Embiid.

LeBron called signing with Philadelphia his "last decision." He's going to MSG for the Knicks' night of nights. The basketball gods wrote this one.

And to cap it off, the Thunder and Spurs — who squared off in the Western Conference Finals last season — get their rematch on the national stage.
